Permission provider from a "permission -> roles" matrix

Source: R/permissions.R
aa_permissions_from_matrix.Rd

Creates a permission provider (provider) for aa_can() and aa_require() from a named list, where the name is a permission and the value is the roles that hold it (a vector or a single string).

Usage

aa_permissions_from_matrix(matrix)

Arguments

matrix

A named list "permission -> roles", or a function without arguments that returns such a list.

Value

A function function(user): for a list with a role field it returns the permission names. For an empty or unknown role it returns character(0).

Details

The administrator role does not receive permissions automatically: a permission is held only by the roles listed in the matrix.

If the matrix changes while the app is running (a permission editor), pass a function without arguments that returns the current matrix, for example function() conf_rv()$access_matrix. It is then read on every check.

A permission provider is any function function(user) that returns a vector of the user's permission names. If a matrix does not suit you (per-user permissions from a database, group-based permissions), write such a function yourself: the other package functions treat it the same way.

Examples

provider <- aa_permissions_from_matrix(list(
  Tasks = c("admin", "user", "viewer"),
  Access = "admin"
))
provider(list(login = "ivan", role = "user"))
#> [1] "Tasks"
aa_can(list(login = "ivan", role = "user"), "Access", provider)
#> [1] FALSE
